html:
Operation Grapple was the series of British nuclear tests held in 1957 and 1958 at Malden Island and Kiritimati (Christmas Island), now part of Kiribati. With them Britain tested its first hydrogen bombs.

Thousands of British, New Zealand and Fijian servicemen took part, and Gilbertese people lived on Kiritimati during the tests. Many veterans later reported illness linked to radiation.

The tests helped restore nuclear cooperation between Britain and the United States, which tested at Kiritimati itself in 1962. They belong to the long story of nuclear testing in the Pacific, from Bikini to Moruroa. See also Maralinga.
